### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6cb744070773ed7c5b1aff90c60d227c047fae07` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2b34db33e8e6b3d0783144082c86bcc850a43f79` — the merge of head `6f38761340f445c5a4e250eab733a5868c07f74c` into base `6cb744070773ed7c5b1aff90c60d227c047fae07`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2b34db33e8e6b3d0783144082c86bcc850a43f79 && git checkout 2b34db33e8e6b3d0783144082c86bcc850a43f79
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6cb744070773ed7c5b1aff90c60d227c047fae07 6f38761340f445c5a4e250eab733a5868c07f74c && git checkout -B drift-repro 6cb744070773ed7c5b1aff90c60d227c047fae07 && git merge --no-ff 6f38761340f445c5a4e250eab733a5868c07f74c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6cb744070773ed7c5b1aff90c60d227c047fae07
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

`Test Core (8/10)` is red on head `b5e72924` because of this PR: `packages/rest/src/meta-item-version-token-occ.test.ts` › "after a publish (no draft row): a held `If-Match` is refused 409 with `currentVersion: null`; `If-None-Match: *` writes the next draft" (got 200, expected 409). Reproduced locally: 1 failed, 14 passed (15).

That arm pins the behaviour this PR removes. It saves draft d1, publishes it unchanged, then saves a new draft pinned with d1's token. The published row now holds d1's body, so the token names the live row and the first draft is accepted, which is the card's acceptance 1. Nothing was overwritten that the caller had not read.

The fix is test-only: split the arm into (a) a held token naming the published body writes the next draft, and (b) a held token the published row moved past is refused 409 `METADATA_CONFLICT` naming the current published version, then `If-None-Match: *` writes the next draft. It is not pushed yet because `packages/rest/**` is outside this order's file surface; waiting on the seat to widen it to that one test file.

## 维护者速读
- 是什么：用轻门改一个已发布、还没有草稿的项时，带着读到的 `version` 作 `ifMatch` 第一次保存不再被 409 拒绝；已发布项在读之后被别人改过，仍然拒绝，并说出当前版本号。
- 影响：实测 12 次改已发布项有 9 次撞上这个拒绝，模型只能去掉 `ifMatch` 绕开乐观锁；修好后 MCP、REST 草稿保存、Studio 三个保存入口一起受益。
- 要你做什么：无。普通队列落地（不在受管面上）。

Seat opinion: land.

## 席位核对

Seat L1 verdict: **ACCEPT** · head `6f38761340f4` · 2026-11-26T18:11Z · `Fixes #37628`.

- **Shape:** draft, base `main`, `Fixes #37628` only; 5 files +163/−8 (fence widened by the seat to `packages/rest/src/meta-item-version-token-occ.test.ts`, recorded on the card); changeset `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` + `@objectstack/runtime` patch, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **Diff read:** `protocol-save.ts:2191-2214`. Only a draft save with a string token and no draft row takes the new path: the token is compared with the active head at the write package, and on a match the draft is written with a `null` parent, so the repository lock still refuses a draft written in between. A moved published row throws through the same `saveConflict` envelope, naming its version. Every other save keeps `currentStored`. Tool text in `mcp-authoring.ts` follows.
- **Clause-② no:** right. The PR quotes the published `ifMatch` text ("refused if the draft changed since"); the old refusal fired with no draft at all, so the fix brings behaviour to the published text, and no new refusal is added.
- **Premise correction accepted:** the comparison lives at `protocol-save.ts` (`storedParentForToken`), not `protocol-save-conflict.ts`, which only builds the 409. Publish and delete callers unaffected.
- **Tests:** served-content-hash 33/33 (ablation: fix removed → 4 red); REST OCC 16/16 with the old "null" case split into accept and refuse-naming-the-version (code + status); runtime mcp-authoring 57/57; metadata-protocol 23444 green; three packages typecheck exit 0 (dev's report on this head).
- **Gates:** head check-runs 39 success / 18 skipped / 0 failed; `mergeable_state` clean.
- **Landing tier:** `check-governed-merges --pr 37651`: 0 of 5 paths governed, 171 lines; `landing-k` OK, K = 3.
